name: Nintendo GameCube
description: Nintendo's 2001 console, its first to use optical discs, small 8 cm discs designed to resist piracy. Its compact, powerful hardware ran games such as Super Smash Bros. Melee, Metroid Prime and The Wind Waker.
curiosities: The Game Boy Player attachment plugs into the bottom to play Game Boy Advance games on a TV.
Panasonic sold the Q, a version that also plays DVDs, only in Japan.
Its graphics chip was designed by ArtX, a company founded by former SGI engineers and bought by ATI.
The Wii, its successor, was built on an evolution of the same hardware and plays GameCube discs.
Its games come on 8 cm optical discs holding about 1.5 GB.
story: After the Nintendo 64's cartridges cost it publishers, Nintendo turned to small optical discs. The GameCube, designed with IBM's Gekko processor and ArtX's Flipper graphics, launched in Japan in September 2001, with a handle on its box.

It was small, fast and easy to develop for, but behind the PlayStation 2 in third-party games and online play. Super Smash Bros. Melee, Metroid Prime, The Wind Waker, Resident Evil 4 at first, Pikmin and Animal Crossing made its library.
It sold about 22 million units. Its controller lives on in Smash Bros., and its hardware became the base of the Wii.
